The promise of green growth lies in turning the next wave of development investment into productive capacity, jobs and higher-value industries in developing countries. That opportunity is within reach, but the task is urgent: over the next 10 to 15 years, 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age, while current trajectories are expected to create only 400 million jobs and the sustainable development financing gap remains around $4 trillion a year.

Agro-value chains show what this can look like in practice. They connect production to higher-value activity after the farmgate, where reliable and affordable clean energy can reduce losses, strengthen SMEs, support local industry and help producer communities retain more value. Agrifood systems use about 30% of globally available energy, with around 70% of that energy used after the farmgate, making clean energy central to inclusive growth.

This week, I look forward to joining the HLPF 2026 side event “Powering Green Growth: Inclusive Solutions for Energy and Industry through Agro-Value Chains,” where we will explore how clean energy, sustainable industrialization and stronger partnerships can advance inclusive economic growth and progress on SDGs 7, 9 and 17.

📅 Wednesday, 8 July 2026 | 🕐 1:15–2:30 PM EDT | 📍 Conference Room 4, UN Headquarters, New York
